scope.description: Control case on the same explicit leadership-transfer path: on a real four-node cluster, name a server that still holds its vote as the transfer target and emit one CA_EVENT JSON line recording the reported transfer error, whether the named target ever reached Leader, which servers led during a bounded interval, the end states of the original leader and the target, and the term before and after.
assumptions: MakeCluster(4, t, nil) with no demotion is the same cluster shape as the vote-less case, so the configuration, the catch-up wait and the TimeoutNow delivery are unchanged and only the target's suffrage differs.
The target is again chosen from nodes in Follower state, so it is a viable replication peer and the transfer routine's catch-up wait can be satisfied.

The control is a same-cause case, not a requirement check: it separates 'transfer works in this harness' from 'a vote-less target cannot take leadership', and its outcome does not by itself settle the attribution of the earlier term movement.

basis.prefix: The harness (draft/assurance_generated_test.go) is one TestAssurance-prefixed test in the captured package, identical to the vote-less-target case except that the target is never demoted. It bootstraps a real four-voter cluster with MakeCluster(4, t, nil), takes the single elected leader via c.Leader(), waits for a follower using c.WaitEvent and c.GetInState, confirms from the leader's latest configuration that the target's suffrage is Voter, samples the maximum current term across c.rafts, calls leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(target.localID, target.localAddr) through the public API and records the error its future reports, then polls every 20 ms for up to 3 s across all nodes in c.rafts recording every address observed in Leader state, whether the named target was ever among them, and whether the original leader led again. It finishes by recording the maximum term after the window and the end states of the original leader and the target, and prints one CA_EVENT line tagged transfer_to_voter so the control event is distinguishable from the vote-less-target event in the same investigation.
